advances: For the exact four-height mixed-gap family, failure of the original same-weight selected-energy baseline is confined to odd a, two heavy levels of full intrinsic dimension n-1, heavy original mass at least 217/256, sufficiently many occupied heavy parity classes, and more than 98/9 cross-level pairs per occupied parity class at height b. The main mechanism is an exact identity comparing the unequal-weight pair deletion with the deviation of all ambient parity masses from uniformity. A divisor-slice argument additionally excludes a lattice-anchored full fundamental parallelepiped in either heavy level. The complementary certified branches have the original-law product moment consumer with one coefficient for the whole product. The remaining geometric deletion-versus-deviation inequality is stated as unproved.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact f1564d15ced22336 supplies the original-mass intrinsic level-energy estimate and the universal same-weight selected-row product moment consumer. All mass, parity-deviation, cross-pair, and divisor-slice assertions used here are proved above.
proof:
Every level is nonempty, every \(p_x\) is positive on \(A\), and \(Z\) is the full original normalizer. Since \(t>0\), exact weight levels and exact height levels coincide. If \(x\in\widehat R_j\), then \(H(2j-x)=H(j)\), so both reflected endpoints have probability \(p_j\). In particular \(\widehat H_p(j)=p_j|\widehat R_j|>0\), the central atom is retained once, and both orientations of a noncentral retained pair are included.

We first record the level capacity and energy estimates, keeping the ambient \(K\). Fix \(s\) and \(u_s\in\mathcal A_s\). The space \(V_s=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal A_s-u_s)\) has dimension \(h_s\le n-1\), since it lies in the real kernel of the nonzero functional \(H\). Its saturated lattice \(\mathcal L_s=V_s\cap\mathbb Z^n\) has rank \(h_s\): the space is spanned by integer vectors, and the rational and real ranks of integer matrices agree. Thus its intrinsic parity quotient has \(2^{h_s}\) elements. Ambient same parity for two points in \(u_s+\mathcal L_s\) is equivalent to intrinsic same parity. Indeed, if \(x-y=2z\) with \(z\in\mathbb Z^n\), then \(z\in V_s\), hence \(z\in\mathcal L_s\). The occupancy assumption therefore gives \(N_s\le2^{h_s+1}\le K\).

The original-mass level estimate of f1564d15ced22336 applies to the globally affine log weight \(-tH\), and gives
$$
 b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge
 \sum_{s\in\lbrace0,a,b,2b\rbrace}\alpha_s^3 4^{-h_s}.
\tag{10}
$$
In particular a level of mass greater than \(3/4\) gives \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}>4(3/4)^3=27/16>1\). This application uses that fact's estimate for exact levels, which imposes no spectral-gap assumption.

Write \(\lambda=e^{-ta}\) and \(\beta=e^{-tb}\); these are raw weight ratios, not arithmetic ranks or row cardinalities. The four raw weights are \(1,\lambda,\beta,\beta^2\), and \(Z=N_0+\lambda N_a+\beta N_b+\beta^2N_{2b}\). The hypotheses imply
$$
 \beta\le\frac1{64},\qquad
 \frac{\lambda}{\beta}
 =\beta^{a/b-1}>\beta^{-3/4}
 \ge64^{3/4}=16\sqrt2>20.
\tag{11}
$$
The final strict comparison follows by squaring: \((16\sqrt2)^2=512>400\). Consequently \(\rho_0>\rho_a>20\rho_b\) and \(\rho_b\ge64\rho_{2b}\). By the level capacities and the activity assumption,
$$
 \alpha_s=\frac{N_s}{K}\rho_s\le\rho_s,\qquad
 A_0=\sum_s\alpha_s\rho_s^2<1,\qquad
 \alpha_s<\rho_s^{-2}.
\tag{12}
$$
Here every \(\rho_s\) is positive, so each last inequality follows from its own nonnegative summand in the preceding strict inequality.

Suppose no \(\rho_s\) belongs to \((1/3,3)\). Since these four ratios are decreasing, let \(k\) be the number that are at least \(3\); all remaining ratios are at most \(1/3\). For the first \(k\) levels use \(\alpha_s<1/9\), and for the others use \(\alpha_s\le\rho_s\) and the gaps in (11). The resulting upper bounds for the total mass are, for \(k=0,1,2,3,4\), respectively,
$$
 \frac{2+1/20+1/1280}{3},\quad
 \frac19+\frac{1+1/20+1/1280}{3},\quad
 \frac29+\frac{1+1/64}{3},\quad
 \frac39+\frac13,\quad \frac49.
\tag{13}
$$
Each number is less than one. For example, in the first two cases the low levels at heights \(a,b,2b\) have ratios bounded by \(1/3,1/60,1/3840\), and in the first case the additional ratio at height zero is at most \(1/3\). In the third case the two remaining ratios are bounded by \(1/3,1/192\). This explains every term, including ratios at the endpoints \(1/3\) and \(3\). Each case contradicts \(\sum_s\alpha_s=1\), proving existence of a moderate ratio.

If \(1/3<\rho_b<3\), then \(\rho_0>\rho_a>20/3\). By (12), \(\alpha_0+\alpha_a<18/400=9/200\), while \(\alpha_{2b}\le\rho_{2b}<3/64\). Hence \(\alpha_b>1-9/200-3/64=1453/1600>3/4\). If instead \(1/3<\rho_{2b}<3\), then \(\rho_b>64/3\) and \(\rho_0>\rho_a>1280/3\). Again (12) gives
\(\alpha_0+\alpha_a+\alpha_b<(9/4096)(1+2/400)<1/4\), so \(\alpha_{2b}>3/4\). Equation (10) proves the positive energy assertion in both cases.

Any failure must therefore have a moderate heavy ratio. Whether it is \(\rho_0\) or \(\rho_a\), one has \(\rho_a<3\). It follows that \(\rho_b<3/20\) and \(\rho_{2b}\le\rho_b/64\). Using (12),
\(\alpha_b+\alpha_{2b}<(3/20)(1+1/64)=39/256\), which proves the first two inequalities in (6) and in particular the mass restriction in (5).

If one of the heavy dimensions is at most \(n-2\), apply the two-term weighted power inequality to (10). Explicitly, for positive \(c_0,c_a\), Hölder gives
\((\alpha_0+\alpha_a)^3\le(\alpha_0^3/c_0^2+\alpha_a^3/c_a^2)(c_0+c_a)^2\). With \(c_s=2^{h_s}\) and \(h_s\le n-1\), this yields
$$
 K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}
 \ge\frac{K^2\alpha_{\mathrm H}^3}{(2^{h_0}+2^{h_a})^2}
 \ge\frac{16}{9}\alpha_{\mathrm H}^3
 \ge\frac{16}{9}\left(\frac{217}{256}\right)^3>1.
\tag{14}
$$
For the middle inequality the denominator is at most \((K/4+K/2)^2\). The final strict inequality is exactly \(163493008>150994944\) after multiplication by positive denominators. For \(n=1\), the dimension condition \(h_s\le n-2\) cannot hold for a nonempty level, so this implication has no exceptional negative-dimensional case. Thus failure requires \(h_0=h_a=n-1\).

Next use completeness to classify all same-parity pairs. Any two same-parity atoms have an integer midpoint in \(Q\), hence in \(A\). For unequal occupied heights, the six possible averages are
\(a/2,b/2,b,(a+b)/2,b+a/2,3b/2\). Under \(0<a<b/4\), only \(b\), from heights \(0,2b\), belongs to the occupied height set. Indeed \(a/2\in(0,a)\), both \(b/2\) and \((a+b)/2\) lie in \((a,b)\), and both \(b+a/2\) and \(3b/2\) lie in \((b,2b)\). Therefore the only possible unequal-height same-parity pairs join heights \(0\) and \(2b\). In particular the two heavy levels occupy disjoint parity classes, and every class occupied by \(\mathcal A_b\) contains points only from that level.

Let \(\mu_{\mathrm H,\eta}=\sum_{x\in A_{\mathrm H}\cap\eta}p_x\). The ordered pairs in the heavy union with equal parity are all within a single height. Their midpoints lie in that height and give exactly the oriented selected row entries centered in the heavy union. Every such entry contributes \(p_j\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}}=p_xp_{2j-x}\), because its three probabilities agree. Consequently
$$
 \sum_{j\in A_{\mathrm H}}p_j\widehat H_p(j)
 =\sum_\eta\mu_{\mathrm H,\eta}^2
 \ge\frac{\alpha_{\mathrm H}^2}{C_{\mathrm H}}.
\tag{15}
$$
All heavy masses and \(C_{\mathrm H}\) are positive. Cauchy--Schwarz on the original heavy center probabilities gives
\((\sum_{j\in A_{\mathrm H}}p_j\widehat H_p(j))^2\le\alpha_{\mathrm H}\sum_{j\in A_{\mathrm H}}p_j\widehat H_p(j)^2\). Together with (15) this proves the last bound in (4). Failure therefore requires \(C_{\mathrm H}>K\alpha_{\mathrm H}^{3/2}\).

If \(a\) is even, both heavy levels have even \(H\)-height. The primitive integer coefficient vector of \(H\) has an odd coefficient, so its induced linear functional on \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\) is nonzero and its kernel has exactly \(K/2\) elements. Thus \(C_{\mathrm H}\le K/2\). In the moderate-heavy case the bound just proved gives \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge4\alpha_{\mathrm H}^3>4(3/4)^3>1\). The moderate-tail cases were already certified. This proves that every failure has odd \(a\), including all parity possibilities for \(b\).

We now prove the exact deletion identity. The map sending a supported oriented row entry \((j,x)\) to the ordered endpoints \((x,2j-x)\) bijects all full row entries with all ordered same-parity pairs: the inverse midpoint belongs to \(A\) by convexity and completeness. Global affinity gives \(p_{(x+y)/2}^2=p_xp_y\), so its contribution to the full first reflected sum is exactly \(p_xp_y\). The selected sum \(\widehat\chi(p)\) keeps exactly the equal-height ordered pairs. By the preceding classification the deleted pairs are the two orientations of the \(J\) unordered \(0\)-to-\(2b\) pairs. Each has probability product
\(Z^{-2}e^{-2tb}=(\rho_b/K)^2\). Therefore
$$
 \widehat\chi(p)=\sum_\eta\mu_\eta^2
 -\frac{2J\rho_b^2}{K^2},\qquad
 \mathcal D=K^2\sum_\eta\mu_\eta^2-K.
\tag{16}
$$
The second equality expands the square using all \(K\) ambient classes and \(\sum_\eta\mu_\eta=1\), including empty classes. These equalities prove the first identity in (4). Cauchy--Schwarz on the full original center law gives \(b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge\widehat\chi(p)^2\), proving its other stated bound. Since \(\widehat\chi(p)>0\), failure of the energy baseline implies \(K\widehat\chi(p)<1\), and (16) then implies \(\mathcal D<2J\rho_b^2\).

In the moderate-heavy case, any class occupied at height \(b\) contains either one or two atoms, all from that height. Its scaled mass is thus \(\rho_b\) or \(2\rho_b\), and is less than \(3/10\). Its contribution to \(\mathcal D\) is at least \(49/100\), whence \(\mathcal D\ge49C_b/100\). Also \(2J\rho_b^2\le9J/200\), including \(J=0\). Substitution into (4) proves the last inequality of (6). Thus \(J\le98C_b/9\) certifies \(K\widehat\chi(p)\ge1\), and hence \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge1\). The moderate-tail cases were already certified, so this sufficient branch holds throughout the stated family. This proves the remaining condition in (5). All other listed positive branches follow from (4), the mass restriction, (14), and the even-\(a\) argument. Equation (4) also proves the sufficient implication (7).

For the geometric exclusion we prove a divisor-slice assertion directly. Choose \(e\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \(H(e)=1\), which exists by primitivity. Then \(\mathbb Z^n=\mathbb Ze\oplus\mathcal L\), since \(x=H(x)e+(x-H(x)e)\) uniquely. In particular \(\mathcal L\) has a lattice basis of \(n-1\) elements. Suppose a convex set contains the parallelepiped \(P=u+\sum_i[0,1]f_i\), with \(H(u)=c\), and a lattice point \(V\) of height \(c+m\), where \(m\) is a positive integer. Write \(V-u=me+\sum_iv_if_i\), with integer \(v_i\). For any positive divisor \(k\) of \(m\), the slice of \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cup\lbrace V\rbrace)\) at height \(c+k\) contains, in fact equals,
$$
 u+ke+\sum_i
 \left[\frac{kv_i}{m},\frac{kv_i}{m}+1-\frac{k}{m}\right]f_i.
\tag{17}
$$
To verify the formula, every point of that convex hull has the form \((1-\theta)z+\theta V\), with \(z\in P\) and \(0\le\theta\le1\); its height is \(c+\theta m\), fixing \(\theta=k/m\). Put \(d=m/k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). Each interval in (17) is \([v_i/d,v_i/d+1-1/d]\) and contains \(\lceil v_i/d\rceil\): the fractional part of \(v_i/d\) is an integer multiple of \(1/d\), so rounding upward moves it by either zero or at most \(1-1/d\). Choosing these integer coefficients independently proves that the slice contains a lattice point. This includes negative \(v_i\), the endpoint \(k=m\), and \(n=1\), when the coefficient sum is empty.

Apply this assertion inside \(Q\), using any \(V\in\mathcal A_{2b}\). A parallelepiped at height zero has \(m=2b\), and both \(k=1\) and \(k=2\) divide \(m\). It would force occupied heights \(1\) and \(2\). Since \(b>4a\) and \(a\ge1\), one has \(b\ge5\); neither forced height equals \(b\) or \(2b\), and at most one equals \(a\). Thus at least one is forbidden. A parallelepiped at height \(a\) has \(m=2b-a\), and \(k=1\) would force height \(a+1\), which lies strictly between \(a\) and \(b\), again forbidden. This proves the exclusion for \(Q\cap H^{-1}(s)\), and hence for \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_s)\subseteq Q\cap H^{-1}(s)\). Conversely, if the former section contained such a parallelepiped, all its integral vertices would belong to \(\mathcal A_s\), so its whole convex hull would be contained in \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_s)\) as well. This also verifies that the two formulations of the exclusion agree. When \(n=1\), any point in \(\mathcal A_0\) itself is the rank-zero parallelepiped, so no such four-height support exists.

For each factor on a certified branch, we have proved \(b_{\mathrm{equal},i}\ge4^{-n_i}\) using its original probabilities. The universal selected-row product inequalities (6) of f1564d15ced22336 apply to these convex complete supports and affine weights, without requiring the level-energy lower bound (10) itself to cross the threshold. They give exactly the first inequalities in (9); multiplying the certified factor baselines gives the second inequalities. Thus no actual-depth tensorization or per-factor coefficient multiplication is assumed.

Finally, (16) makes (7) equivalent to \(K\widehat\chi(p)\ge1\), while the only general comparison to the selected energy used here is \(b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge\widehat\chi(p)^2\). More explicitly, \(b_{\mathrm{equal}}=\widehat\chi(p)^2+\operatorname{Var}_p(\widehat H_p)\). Thus a strict deficit in the first selected reflected sum does not by itself imply an energy deficit. No estimate supplied above proves (7) for the remaining class; its status and the stated limitation therefore follow with precisely the indicated direction of implication.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\), let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, and suppose \(A=Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is finite, nonempty, and has affine dimension \(n\). Suppose each class of \(\mathbb Z^n/2\mathbb Z^n\) contains at most two points of \(A\). Let \(H:\mathbb Z^n\to\mathbb Z\) be a primitive integer linear functional, meaning \(H(\mathbb Z^n)=\mathbb Z\), and use the same symbol for its real-linear extension. Suppose its occupied heights are exactly \(\lbrace0,a,b,2b\rbrace\), where \(a,b\) are positive integers satisfying \(\gcd(a,b)=1\) and \(0<a<b/4\). Let \(t>0\) satisfy \(tb\ge\log64\) and \(ta<\log64\). Retain the full original law
$$
 w_x=e^{-tH(x)},\qquad Z=\sum_{x\in A}w_x,\qquad
 p_x=w_x/Z,\qquad K=2^n,
 \qquad A_0=K^2\sum_{x\in A}p_x^3<1.
\tag{1}
$$
Extend \(p\) by zero off \(A\). To distinguish height-zero points from the atomic quantity \(A_0\), write \(\mathcal A_s=\lbrace x\in A:H(x)=s\rbrace\), \(N_s=|\mathcal A_s|\), \(h_s=\dim(\operatorname{aff}\mathcal A_s)\), and \(\alpha_s=N_se^{-ts}/Z\), for \(s\in\lbrace0,a,b,2b\rbrace\). Thus these \(h_s,\alpha_s\) are the intrinsic level dimensions and original level masses called \(h_k,\alpha_k\) in accepted fact f1564d15ced22336, with levels indexed by height. Put \(A_{\mathrm H}=\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_a\), \(\alpha_{\mathrm H}=\alpha_0+\alpha_a\), and \(\rho_s=Ke^{-ts}/Z\).

Use precisely the selected-row hats of f1564d15ced22336:
$$
\begin{aligned}
 R_j&=\lbrace x\in A:2j-x\in A\rbrace,&
 \widehat R_j&=\lbrace x\in R_j:H(x)=H(j)\rbrace,\\
 \widehat H_p(j)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat R_j}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},&
 b_{\mathrm{equal}}&=\widehat b(p):=\sum_{j\in A}p_j\widehat H_p(j)^2,\\
 \widehat\chi(p)&=\sum_{j\in A}p_j\widehat H_p(j).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$
In particular \(b_{\mathrm{equal}}\) is an alias for the same-weight selected energy, and is not the full-row energy. All center probabilities, the full \(Z\), and all central row entries remain in these definitions.

For every ambient parity class \(\eta\in\mathbb Z^n/2\mathbb Z^n\), including the empty classes, define its original mass \(\mu_\eta=\sum_{x\in A\cap\eta}p_x\), and put
$$
 \mathcal D=\sum_\eta(K\mu_\eta-1)^2,\qquad
 C_{\mathrm H}=|\lbrace\eta:A_{\mathrm H}\cap\eta\ne\varnothing\rbrace|,
 \qquad C_b=|\lbrace\eta:\mathcal A_b\cap\eta\ne\varnothing\rbrace|.
\tag{3}
$$
Let \(J\) be the number of unordered pairs with one endpoint in \(\mathcal A_0\), one in \(\mathcal A_{2b}\), and both endpoints in the same ambient parity class. Then the following identity and bounds hold:
$$
 K\widehat\chi(p)
 =1+\frac{\mathcal D-2J\rho_b^2}{K},\qquad
 b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge\widehat\chi(p)^2,\qquad
 b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge\frac{\alpha_{\mathrm H}^3}{C_{\mathrm H}^2}.
\tag{4}
$$

If \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}<1\), then all of the following necessary conditions hold:
$$
\begin{gathered}
 \alpha_{\mathrm H}\ge\frac{217}{256},\qquad
 a\text{ is odd},\qquad h_0=h_a=n-1,\\
 C_{\mathrm H}>K\alpha_{\mathrm H}^{3/2},\qquad
 J>\frac{98}{9}C_b,\qquad
 \rho_b<\frac3{20},\qquad \mathcal D<2J\rho_b^2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{5}
$$
More specifically, at least one of \(\rho_0,\rho_a,\rho_b,\rho_{2b}\) lies in \((1/3,3)\). If \(\rho_b\) or \(\rho_{2b}\) lies in this interval, a single level has mass greater than \(3/4\), and \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}>1\). In the remaining case at least one heavy ratio \(\rho_0,\rho_a\) lies in that interval, and
$$
 \alpha_{\mathrm H}>\frac{217}{256},\qquad
 \rho_b<\frac3{20},\qquad
 K\widehat\chi(p)\ge1+\frac{98C_b-9J}{200K}.
\tag{6}
$$
Consequently \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}\ge1\) whenever at least one of these conditions holds: \(\alpha_{\mathrm H}<217/256\); \(a\) is even; one of \(h_0,h_a\) is at most \(n-2\); \(C_{\mathrm H}\le K\alpha_{\mathrm H}^{3/2}\); or \(J\le98C_b/9\). Independently, the inequality
$$
 \mathcal D\ge2J\rho_b^2
\tag{7}
$$
also suffices for that energy baseline by (4).

There is a geometric exclusion valid for every support in the statement, without assuming energy failure. Put \(\mathcal L=\ker H\cap\mathbb Z^n\). For either \(s=0\) or \(s=a\), neither \(Q\cap H^{-1}(s)\) nor \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_s)\) contains a lattice-anchored closed full fundamental parallelepiped
$$
 u+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}[0,1]f_i,
 \qquad u\in\mathbb Z^n,\quad H(u)=s,
\tag{8}
$$
where \(f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1}\) is a lattice basis of \(\mathcal L\). The rank-zero convention makes (8) the point \(u\) when \(n=1\); in particular the four-height family is empty in dimension one.

For the immediate product consequence, let \(L\ge1\) be an integer and let \(p_i\), \(1\le i\le L\), be laws in possibly different ambient dimensions \(n_i\), each satisfying the hypotheses above and at least one certified branch just stated, including (7) when it is known for that factor. Set \(P=\bigotimes_i p_i\) and \(N=\sum_i n_i\), retaining the original product law and normalizers. For the actual ambient closed-halfspace depth \(\tau_P(X)=\inf_{\mathcal H\ni X}P(\mathcal H)\), where the infimum ranges over closed halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^N\), and \(M_s(P)=\sum_XP_X\tau_P(X)^s\), one has
$$
 M_2(P)\ge\frac14\prod_i b_{\mathrm{equal},i}\ge\frac14 4^{-N},
 \qquad
 M_3(P)\ge\frac18\left(\prod_i b_{\mathrm{equal},i}\right)^{3/2}
 \ge\frac18 8^{-N}.
\tag{9}
$$
The coefficients are paid once for the entire product.

Inequality (7) is not proved here for the residual geometric class with \(\alpha_{\mathrm H}\ge217/256\), odd \(a\), \(h_0=h_a=n-1\), \(C_{\mathrm H}>K\alpha_{\mathrm H}^{3/2}\), \(J>98C_b/9\), \(\rho_b<3/20\), and the exclusion (8). Establishing it on that class would rule out all remaining energy failures by (4). It is a sufficient condition, not a claimed necessary condition for the energy baseline: its strict reversal is equivalent to \(K\widehat\chi(p)<1\), and is only necessary for \(K^2b_{\mathrm{equal}}<1\). No energy baseline for all four-height laws, universal arithmetic moment hypothesis, or conclusion for the locked conjecture is asserted.
